adversarial-research-protocol.reason: The independence check is the batch's main result. Wheels for Wellbeing (Co-1) states the same 50m interval as the DfT standard, which reads as lived-experience corroboration; its reference list shows it cites Inclusive Mobility (2021). Treating it as a second data point would double-count one figure across two tiers. Recorded so the interval anchors at the weak band only, while the need it serves anchors at full band.

search_executions.language values written by PRIOR sessions were modified (57 rows normalised from lowercase to uppercase). — Not an evidence edit. v_coverage_priority suppresses a queue cell via se.language = ljm.language and SQLite compares TEXT case-sensitively, so 57 of 68 logged searches were never suppressing their own coverage cells and the priority queue was reporting completed work as un-done. The normalisation changes no claim, tier, figure or finding. Disclosed here and in the session file because touching another session's rows warrants disclosure even when mechanical.

scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py — an enforcement gate — was edited by the same session it was gating. — R5 compared `language <> 'en'` against a column carrying uppercase ISO codes, so it failed this batch spuriously while a genuinely non-English grey search would be caught only by luck of the writer's casing. Fixed to compare case-insensitively. The risk of a gated session editing its own gate is real, so it is bounded: the blocking --selftest was re-run and still rejects the synthetic violating corpus on R5, proving the check was narrowed rather than defanged.

bias_direction: The pull in a first-ever batch on an empty slug is yield-inflation: eight admissions and a clause-cited standard make the slug look solved, and the tidiest story is 'the evidence supports 50m'. The specific temptations were to count Wheels for Wellbeing's 50m as Co-1 corroboration of the DfT 50m (two tiers agreeing, when it is one figure restated), to promote REF-00947 to Co-1 because its participants are disabled people, and to call REF-00948 T1 because it is an RCT. Each was resolved against the flattering reading and the reasoning written onto the row. The batch's headline result is consequently a negative one: the need is evidenced, the number everyone cites is not.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: A reviewer could argue the independence finding is overstated — Wheels for Wellbeing is a disabled people's organisation applying lived-experience judgment when it endorses 50m, so its agreement is not merely a restatement, and demoting the interval to the weak band discards genuine Co-1 assent. The response is that WfW's own reference list cites Inclusive Mobility (2021) for that figure, so the corpus cannot distinguish independent endorsement from citation; where a Co-1 source visibly derives a number from a standard, the honest record is one figure at its original strength plus a note that a Co-1 organisation did not dispute it. A second reviewer could argue that admitting ASLA at all pollutes the corpus with a known-bad figure; the counter is that an unflagged bad figure in wide circulation is more dangerous outside the corpus than inside it with a MISMATCH grade attached. A third could argue this batch should have declared the whole slug blocked on non-English vocabulary rather than proceeding EN-only; that is recorded as a deferral with reason, not a completed axis.
